title: Dockerfiles must declare a non-root USER before the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT

source.excerpt: Heads up team — starting Nov 1, every Dockerfile needs to declare a non-root `USER` before the final `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT`. Container Security flagged this in the latest audit: several images are still running as root by default. Please add a `USER` directive (not UID 0) to your Dockerfiles before the cutover — after Nov 1 this becomes a required check.

rules.description: Every Dockerfile must contain a USER directive so the image does not run as root by default. Flags Dockerfiles with no USER instruction at all.

autofix.instructions:
Add a non-root USER directive to this Dockerfile before the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Typical pattern:

  RUN addgroup --system app && adduser --system --ingroup app app
  # ... build/install steps that need root ...
  USER app
  ENTRYPOINT ["..."]

Ensure any paths the process writes to (logs, caches, tmp dirs) are chowned to that user, and that no privileged port (<1024) is bound. Do not use UID 0. Rebuild and run the image locally to confirm it still starts.

rules.verify: docker build -q -t policy-nonroot-check . && u=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.User}}' policy-nonroot-check) && [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != "root" ] && [ "${u%%:*}" != "0" ]

rules.description: The effective (last) USER directive in the Dockerfile must not be root or UID 0. A transient 'USER root' for install steps is allowed as long as a later USER switches to a non-root account.

autofix.instructions:
The last USER directive in this Dockerfile resolves to root/UID 0, so the container runs as root. Create or reference a non-root account and switch to it after the privileged build steps:

  RUN addgroup --system app && adduser --system --ingroup app app
  USER app

Keep any 'USER root' only around steps that genuinely require it, and switch back before the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Verify file ownership and port bindings after the change.

rules.verify: docker build -q -t policy-nonroot-check . && u=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.User}}' policy-nonroot-check) && [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != "root" ] && [ "${u%%:*}" != "0" ]

notes:
Two distinct obligations: (1) a USER directive must exist, (2) it must not be UID 0/root. Severity is blocking because the announcement states this 'becomes a required check' after the cutover; deadline 2026-11-01 is stated explicitly (year resolved from the 2026-10-10 posting date).

Limitations worth reviewing:
- The 'before the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT' ordering requirement is only partially expressible in a single regex. Rule 2 approximates the effective user by checking that no non-root USER appears after a root USER, but it cannot tell whether the last USER precedes the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT in multi-stage builds, nor which stage is the final one. A Dockerfile whose last stage inherits a non-root USER from a base image (no explicit USER anywhere) will be flagged by rule 1 as a false positive; the verify command distinguishes these cases by inspecting the built image's effective user.
- Multi-stage builds where an early stage ends on 'USER root' and the final stage sets a non-root use…
